notes.title: [BETA] Update 0.8.50.18EA
notes.notes:
[p]We’ve reworked the story elements freshness system so it better serves its intended purpose while being less confusing and annoying.
First, the system is now more forgiving: elements lose freshness more slowly and regain it more quickly.
Second and most importantly, everything is now more transparent and easier to track. A clear scale shows you exactly when an element will move to a fresher or staler category, and additional UI elements notify you every time it happens. No more unpleasant surprises.[/p][p][/p][p]But wait, there's more![/p][p][/p][list][*][p]You can now dig up dirt, put a hook in, and search for shady preferences on screenwriters, composers, and editors.[/p][/*][*][p]Bobby Martin has now, once and for all, cast off the very last traces of modesty and will absolutely, unconditionally, definitively, reliably, and without fail accept his favorite gift.[/p][/*][*][p]Ryan Doyle will meet with representatives of another one of your friends. Who knows how this meeting will end?[/p][/*][*][p]Now, if you order a murder from your Irish friends, it will actually end in death. notes.title: The beta testing of “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” Update has begun
notes.notes:
[p]The beta version of the major update is now available on a separate Steam branch, and any owner of the game can join in! [/p][p]
[/p][p]To switch to beta branch, do the following: Right-click the game in your Steam library -> Select Properties -> Select Betas -> Choose the beta branch from the dropdown -> The game will now update to the 'beta' branch (version 0.8.50.1EA or higher is what you’re looking for).[/p][p]
[/p][p]Please note that the beta is currently available in English only. Localizations are on the way and will be added soon.

We deeply appreciate everyone willing to help us test and polish the updated version of the game, but we want to stress once again that this is a beta that we intend to update daily. If you’d prefer to jump straight into the final version of the update, you can simply wait until it moves to the default branch — which is expected to happen in two weeks.

While mentioning every single minor change and addition would turn into an unwieldy mess, here’s the list of things we consider the most significant:

[/p][list][*][p]The Security Department upgrade tree has been completely overhauled. Functions, their distribution across buildings, and the order in which they unlock are much clearer and more transparent now.[/p][/*][*][p]The department popup has also been completely redesigned. Keeping track of current agent assignments, starting them, and canceling them is now much simpler and more convenient.[/p][/*][*][p]Security agents now feel much more like the rest of your staff. They have personal dossiers, can be fired, can ask for a raise, and receive gifts.[/p][/*][*][p]Security agents can now be sent to training.[/p][/*][*][p]Passive protection was too confusing, so now protection is only active and permanent: an agent will guard an employee until you tell them to stop.[/p][/*][*][p]Surveillance is now split into two separate actions: digging up dirt and uncovering illicit preferences. This way it’s clearer and more convenient.[/p][/*][*][p]Compromising material now allows you to instantly poach an employee from another studio without waiting for their current contract to expire. However, studios may sue you for unfair competition.[/p][/*][*][p]If you uncover illicit preferences of employees at other studios and give them an appropriate gift, you can “hook” them, ensuring that once their current contract expires, they will come to you first before considering other offers.[/p][/*][*][p]Competitors can now poach your employees as well. Your security agents can protect them.[/p][/*][*][p]Now, if someone attacks your employees in any way, you’ll always know who ordered it.[/p][/*][*][p]If an agent has compromised themselves with an employee, that agent can no longer surveil them.[/p][/*][*][p]A new category of secrets added: “Ongoing Crime.” It cannot be fully erased while the wrongdoing continues, it can only be contained for now.[/p][/*][*][p]The maximum ratings for both a script and the film made from it now depend on the number of story elements used. Only truly well-developed stories can now aim for widespread acclaim — which, in turn, encourages more complex plot combinations instead of exploiting simplistic pairings.[/p][/*][*][p]After a certain point in the game, story elements will begin to “wear out,” meaning audiences will lose interest in characters and events you use too often. So it will now be much more important to seek out new elements and experiment with fresh stories.[/p][/*][*][p]The maximum possible ratings are now capped at 10.[/p][/*][*][p]The release preparation screen is way more informative now. In particular, you can now see the effectiveness of your ad campaign week by week, and much more. [/p][/*][*][p]Not all advertising options are available by default anymore, some need to be unlocked.[/p][/*][*][p]Choosing advertising options has become more important, “more” now definitely does not mean “better”. [/p][/*][*][p]The list of Alliance initiatives has been updated: some of the meaningless ones were removed, and some more interesting ones were added.[/p][/*][*][p]Competitors are now more aggressive in proposing initiatives.[/p][/*][*][p]Thanks to some UI improvements, it’s now easier to keep track of story elements prohibited by the Code.[/p][/*][*][p]Several new upgrades are added to various departments. For example, you can now terminate employee contracts early and even recover part of the contract cost, or make your departments generate Influence Points/Reputation instead of researching.[/p][/*][*][p]New characters are now generated more frequently and with greater variety. Moreover, if low-skilled characters remain un-hired for a long time, they leave the show business, making way for newcomers.[/p][/*][*][p]Ratings and box office performance of competitor films now depend more clearly on script quality, involved talent, and invested resources — in other words, their simulation has become more authentic. [/p][/*][*][p]Now, once you’ve fully developed one of the Policies, you face a choice: stick with it to get additional challenges and bonuses in future Acts, or explore other Policies, like it used to be, but without the ability to deepen them later.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now throw parties to please your subordinates or host banquets to earn Influence Points. [/p][/*][*][p]The theater management screen has become more informative. Also, over time, more independent cinemas appear in the game, which you can purchase.[/p][/*][*][p]Persuading department heads to get involved in questionable activities is now transparent and tied to Loyalty.[/p][/*][*][p]Filming and sound recording equipment now becomes obsolete: after some time, manufacturers stop supporting old technologies, so you need to invest in licensing new ones — or develop your own.[/p][/*][*][p]The list of locations for many settings has been updated.[/p][/*][*][p]You now choose which films you want to submit for the Pollux in each category. Additionally, you can invest extra resources to promote your contenders.[/p][/*][*][p]If none of your films are nominated for the Pollux, you can choose not to attend the ceremony — though industry peers will likely see this as a sign of disrespect. But screw them, right?[/p][/*][*][p]Now each addict is associated with a specific type of drug. By the way, we’ve added one more — amphetamine. [/p][/*][*][p]Gift ordering now works differently: gifts arrive in batches rather than one by one. The larger the batch, the less time it takes to prepare each individual gift.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a bunch of new scandals.[/p][/*][*][p]Added 32 new story elements. [/p][/*][*][p]Added 1500 new posters. [/p][/*][*][p]Added 40 new production events. [/p][/*][*][p]Added a number of special events. Without giving too much away, let’s say you’ll get to meet a couple of characters who will play a significant role in Act 2, among other things.[/p][/*][*][p]A major rebalance of pretty much the entire game. In some cases, this is due to a more accurate reflection of historical context, but more often it’s aimed at smoothing the difficulty curve and ensuring the game provides a fair challenge throughout the entire Act. Department burn rates, prices, taxes, staff requests, the impact of various factors on movie ratings and box office — among many, many other things — have all been revised.[/p][/*][/list][p]

Thank you and have fun![/p]

notes.title: Steam Summer Sale and “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” Details
notes.notes:
[p]Hello!
[/p][p]If you’re thinking about picking up Hollywood Animal, you can grab it at 20% off during the Steam Summer Sale, from June 26 to July 10. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/0b46bca3e69b37c70d153fe33ab7323b1ee9333f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]And if you already own the game and are looking forward to what’s next, we’d like to share a quick word on “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” — the big update we’re currently working on. While we won’t be able to finish it by the end of June as we initially hoped, things are moving along nicely, and we’re confident that you’ll enjoy how big and juicy it’s shaping up to be. We’ll announce the date a bit later. And don’t forget that anyone interested will be able to try out the updated version of the game a bit earlier (on a separate branch) and help us with polishing.[/p][p]If this is your first time hearing about “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of”, we recommend checking out [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2680550/view/543356943483273739"][u]this post[/u][/url]. And today, we’d like to share a few additional details.[/p][p][/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/14b1173332cb7f239a3236b7606a332bdcc4d4f0.png"][/img][/p][p]
[b]Pollux algorithms will become more consistent and logical, but that's not all[/b]: now you'll get to choose which films to put forward for consideration in each category, and you'll be able to invest additional resources into promoting them. You can even skip the ceremony if your flicks are snubbed — yes, at the cost of your reputation, but sometimes you just have to show those snobs what you [i]really[/i] think of them!

[b]We're not only redesigning the security department and its features, but also will let you send agents for training[/b] — and in different ways: you can either unlock this option through the revamped upgrade tree or make use of one of your friends' services (guess which friend we’re talking about here). But the cost, duration, and effectiveness will vary.

[b]The tax rate will change both during the first act and throughout the rest of the game[/b]. And, just like in real life, taxes will be especially harsh during WW2.

[b]At some point, two of your friends will get into a serious conflict[/b]: without giving too much away, let's just say they have slightly different visions for the future of Europe. You can take sides, or you can try to reconcile them — but doing so will require significant effort.

[b]You can’t unlock all the new story elements through research alone[/b]. One specific set will only be available as a reward from a new character.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]You’ll have the opportunity to send your post-production staff on six-month courses abroad. [/b]If you’re not too concerned about them coming back not only with new skills, but with new beliefs as well.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Wouldn’t it be nice to honor the memory of Joe Duvall somehow?[/b] It might be wise to save a small corner of your lot just for that.

[b]Have you ever noticed that little patch of land that clearly [i]should[/i] have been part of your lot, but is occupied by some shabby old house[/b]? You’ll get the chance to meet its owner — and that’s just the beginning of your story with the guy. 
[/p][p][b]The Alliance initiatives are getting a refresh[/b]: some rather pointless ones will be removed, while more useful ones will be added. More importantly, other studios will be using them a lot more often.
[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/4340e8d013bbdf495a145b41d936312a6c669968.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]After the release of “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” we’ll also update our roadmap: it’s clearly outdated, but we’d like to wrap up the current big thing first so we can give you more accurate information about what’s coming next and when.


As always, thank you! [/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” Upcoming Major Update (plus 0.8.26EA)
notes.notes:
Hello!

Update 0.8.26EA
- Fixed a problem with an “empty” pre production screen for some save files. 
- Fixed an issue where a movie that didn't get any reviews could lock up the game. 


But of course we're not here today just for such a minor update. It's May, so we decided to tell you a little bit more about what we are working on and how the game will change in the near future. Many of you have seen our roadmap, but it was rather superficial and only outlined our general plans as we saw them before the start of Early Access. 

We've been following your feedback closely, reading thousands of posts and emails and watching hundreds of hours of streams and videos. And we have come to the conclusion that the small additions we have planned for the coming months for Act 1, while we are working on Act 2, just won’t be enough. Act 1 needs not only new content, but serious systemic improvements, and we're already hard at work on them.

We'll continue to release regular patches with bugfixes and minor improvements, but the bigger changes will come in one big update. For a while we called it “The Super Update”, but when it came time to decide on a name, “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” seemed quite appropriate. 

Here’s a very brief overview of what we're cooking. 


[h1]Complete rebalancing[/h1]
 
The difficulty curve will become smoother, and there will be virtually no prices, bonuses, or any other values in the game that won't be revised. It will be easier to survive the first few years and get used to the basic mechanics, but after that the game will require you to watch your spending more carefully and use all the tools more efficiently. The struggle to make each movie profitable will become more tangible. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/b43cea26dfdb70b9ac40bf397f1e1a5258c2e2bf.png[/img]


[h1]Scripts will now work a little differently[/h1]

The game will encourage you to find and effectively use new story elements and constantly put together fresh and increasingly complex story combinations.

First, the final result will depend a bit more heavily on how well you put the elements together. 

Second, the maximum score of the script will be limited by the number of elements you use -- which, in turn, will limit the maximum score of the future movie. It will take effort to make a truly outstanding script. 

Third, story elements will now “wear out” from frequent use and will be less likely to attract an audience for a while. 

These and a few other changes will increase your engagement in putting stories together, but more importantly, good results will feel more deserved and rewarding. An 8 point movie would be an impressive outcome. A 9 point movie would be an incredible accomplishment. A 10 point movie would be a sensation. And all of these updated rules will apply to your competitors just the same. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/92fec158b47c0cf727422ee5c8a5f754db2b0ec6.png[/img]


[h1]Redesigned security department[/h1]

In the current version of the game, the usefulness of agents is often not very clear, and the progression within the department is quite confusing. 

Not only have we made things clearer, but we've also added new functionality. 

For example, if you find compromising material on an employee of a rival studio (and a lot more people will now keep secrets), you can use this as leverage to instantly poach them to your studio. And if you found out what illegal gift an employee of a rival studio prefers and gave it to them, they will automatically come to you with an offer when their current contract expires. 

But there is another side to this: competitors will become more aggressive and learn the same tricks. So the department's role in the game will increase dramatically. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/3c6fe254d9fce4e00e1fd36048bf5ff0688b9415.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/a6cd32f628084eb9da6e54bdf73a79edacd38a3d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/000fb8872e38c34f589ffbd9db1d8c456bb92338.png[/img]


[h1]Parties [/h1]

It may seem like a small thing in the big picture, but still, Hollywood isn't really Hollywood without parties. After all, it's a great way to make everyone happy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/6c14fd246d95620d7205459a9478d1b31b302ce7.png[/img]


[h1]100+ new events[/h1]

Incidents at various stages of production, new scandals, new legal entanglements, and even a chance to find out who puts out the Bonegrinder paper. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/3bf5df95c29174f3e5c33b5fd3221228c76d95b7.png[/img]


[h1]Many QoL improvements and enhancements[/h1]

We're making more transparent and friendly all those elements of the game that are now confusing or just plain annoying, and we're also fixing many UI glitches and adding additional explanations wherever they're needed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/6d0df0553ed89d9ac9f2f2c52e7d5af42c79565a.png[/img]

The update is still several weeks away from being ready -- so expect it in June rather than May -- and will contain a lot more stuff than we've listed. But we decided to share the first details as early as possible so you can get a better idea of what direction the game is heading in. 

About a week before the release “The Stuff That Dreams Are Made Of” will become available on a separate test branch for anyone who wants to help us with testing. So stay tuned!

Thank you!

notes.title: Hotfix 0.8.8EA
notes.notes:
Hello!

Thank you very much for playing Hollywood Animal! We appreciate your feedback and we’re working hard to address as many issues as humanly possible, as fast as we can. 

Here are some of the things from this update, as well as a few words about our plans for the coming days.

[h2][b]Bugfixes:[/b][/h2]

- Fixed a serious problem that would cause a movie to get stuck in various stages of filmmaking. 
- Fixed a problem that could freeze the game on an empty release popup. 
- Fixed a problem that could cause the game to show you an empty hiring screen. 
- Fixed a problem that could cause the game to get stuck during the Policies introduction. 
- Fixed a problem that could freeze the game when you interact with the Pollux nominations popup. 
- Fixed a problem that could freeze time due to a glitch in the windows queue. 
- Dead screenwriters can’t write scripts anymore. 
- And a bunch of smaller fixes like a missing story element icon. 


[h2][b]Balance improvements:[/b][/h2]


We made a number of tweaks that made the game less unforgiving. 

- Utilities now cost about 50% less
- General staff now costs about 20% less
- Reduced time for some upgrades
- Using your own sound studio, concert hall, and printing office in post production costs $0 (because if you have them, you’re already paying for them)
- You start the game with $7.6 million 


[i][b]Unfortunately, most of the changes, including major bugfixes, are only applicable to the new game and cannot be applied to save files. So, if you’ve faced significant issues, we ask that you start a new run. [/b][/i]


[h2][b]What's cooking in the upcoming updates?[/b][/h2]

In addition to further bugfixes and balance improvements, we are currently working on the following features: 

- Animations of production screens and negotiations will speed up significantly after multiple plays. Also you’ll be able to extend contracts with executives without using the negotiations screen. 

- You’ll be able to skip the tutorial.  

- When you for whatever reason lose your department head, the department upgrade will be paused instead of cancelled.

notes.title: Q&A session with Hollywood Animal developers
notes.notes:
Hi all!

Recently, we ran a Q&A session in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/qJmkdg973s]Discord server[/url]. We picked the most interesting questions and answered them. Please see below. 

But before that, here's a quick reminder: Hollywood Animal will be available on Steam Early Access on January 16, 2025. 
The demo version will be available this December. 

Wishlist and follow the Steam page: 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2680550/Hollywood_Animal/

Watch the most recent Hollywood Animal trailer 'A box of spiders disguised as a tycoon game':
[previewyoutube=oDFPTtGHyno;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Can we make propaganda films or political films?[/b] 
Yes, there will be story elements related to politics, and certain moments in the game will allow you to participate in creating propaganda.

[b]Will we be able to make TV shows later in the game?[/b] 
At the moment, we don't have plans for TV shows or animation, because with the level of detail we've chosen for this game, it's going to be an insane amount of work. We're going to focus on movies for now. But these are great ideas for potential DLCs in the future.

[b]When it comes to sequels/franchises will we have the option to kill off characters?[/b] 
Pick “Protagonist Dies Heroically” for the ending and then don’t bring them back for the sequel, and voilà, they're dead!

[b]Will we have the option to licence existing stories in the world to make movies?[/b] 
It's not something that will be available in the game from the start, but we plan to add franchises in one of the first major updates during Early Access, and yes, you will be able to licence books/comics/radio shows and adapt them into films.

[b]Will we be able to "change" historical events?[/b] 
You can postpone certain events or nudge them in a certain direction, and you can certainly rewrite the history of the movie industry. But you can't avoid something as big as, for example, WW2.

[b]Have you chosen early access in part to allow you to increase the scope of the game? Or has the vision always been similar since the start of the demo?[/b] 
The overall concept of the game has always remained the same, but it’s true that our appetites and ambitions have grown considerably during development. You always want to add a little more and make something a little better. The positive response to the demo gave us some confidence, but more importantly showed us that people are interested in playing as deep and varied a game as possible. So we’ve committed to delivering such a game, even if it will take more work and more time than we once thought.

[b]Will the factions you interact with change over time, or between eras?[/b] 
Yes, throughout the game you will have chances to make new friends as well as lose old ones.

[b]Can we drive enemy studios into bankruptcy to take the lead in "the Animal Kingdom"?[/b] 
You can hurt other studios significantly in Act 1, but, without revealing too much, it's safe to say that things are going to get more brutal in Act 2.

[b]If we can sell technology to others, can we buy technology from others?[/b] 
You can buy technology from companies that specialize in it.

[b]Will it be possible to order not only police raids, but also a mafia raid, which could completely destroy the studio?[/b] 
Mafia provides slightly different but equally useful services!

[b]Are there going to be more locations for the movies or just the 5 that appeared in the demo?[/b] 
If you're referring to settings, then of course there will be way more than 5.

[b]Surprised this isn't here, but can we demolish buildings?[/b] 
Yes!

[b]Will distribution ever branch out beyond just the US?[/b] 
International business will be one of the main features of Act 2, but Act 1 will also provide some opportunities to show movies abroad (ahem-nazis-ahem).

[b]Is the "devil's cauldron" for cooking up trash elements ONLY for studios with the "Trash Dealer" type?[/b]
Yes.

[b]And will the soundtrack change over the years to the one that was popular during those years?[/b] 
The soundtrack will change over the years, not necessarily to something popular during those years (although that too), but rather to something that we feel characterizes the true nature of the period.

[b]Do you plan on establishing a beta testers group - inner circle testing rounds before Early Access updates?[/b] 
Yes, stay tuned!

[b]Will there be an endless mode?[/b] 
We plan to add an endless mode at the same time as Act 2.

[b]Will there be achievements during EA?[/b] 
Yes.

[b]Are there any plans to have Steam Workshop support for modding purposes?[/b] 
Yes, but only after we implement all the things we've planned for Acts 1-3.

[b]When can we expect an Act 2 release after the initial EA release date?[/b] 
Act 2 is scheduled for the summer.


Thank you for your attention!

[i]P.S. You are free to ask us any questions about the game in [url=https://discord.com/invite/qJmkdg973s]Discord[/url]; we will make Q&A sessions like this again in the future.[/i]

notes.title: New mechanics and features
notes.notes:
Hello!

A big thank you to everyone who played the demo for Hollywood Animal -- and in case you haven't, you have until August 31st!

Of course, the full game will offer lots more mechanics and features. Today we'd like to talk about a few of them.


[b]Studio Policy[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/2db671287a76b360568bba06645943c46f930fe2.png[/img]

The first few years of Hollywood Animal are spent getting to know the basics and trying to navigate the strange world of the movie business. Once you've settled into your personal play style, you'll have the chance to choose a Studio Policy. Aspire to become a major studio or a trash king, a boutique arthouse studio or an efficient mid-budget film factory.

Studio Policy isn't just about passive bonuses and a new building on the map. It also opens exclusive mechanics, from the intensive promotion of film stars, to making a film in a single week about a robber whose body is covered in penises. (And who among us can say the latter endeavor is less worthy?) As always, the game doesn't insist on anything; you can choose not to choose a Policy, and develop in all directions at once. Still, success is most often achieved by those who know what they're after.


[b]The Alliance[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/6b3b88977da2cf24bf7ce592d626ddf3d6065a4a.png[/img]

Regulate thyself, or be regulated. The Film Studios Alliance of America sets the rules by which the industry operates. What story elements will mark off as too liable to incur the wrath of the public and the government? How many films can be released per year? Shall we agree to cap actor salaries and advertising budgets? Depending on the style of play you choose, very different rules may benefit you. Use your influence to push your own agenda -- or undermine your competitors.

… Or spit in the Alliance's face, resign your membership, and bow to no one's whims! The path of the outcast is incredibly difficult, but it offers rare rewards.


[b]New friends[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/84370a5abcca32e2ebcade819b23435b63f86b7d.png[/img]

Should you get mixed up with the Italian mafia, if you're already friends with the Irish? Is it best to help the prosecutor become mayor, since he's set on ridding the city of gangs and corruption? Is it really so scary to cooperate with the Third Reich, if World War II hasn't even begun yet? Is it wise to marginalize the Ku Klux Klan if many of its members are devoted moviegoers?

The more characters you meet, the more tangled the thicket of mutual benefits and risks.


[b]Proprietary technology[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/32b0a30fd684e0b2a136ca69b6475a5a9f71c917.png[/img]

Not only can you upgrade technologies, you can also invent your own. Why depend on third-party manufacturers? Carefully choose your technology's features, don't skimp on the research budget -- and if the circumstances are right, you might create a camera that's a decade ahead of the competition!

Then you can decide whether to sell your miracle invention to your competitors, or favor a long-term advantage over an immediate profit.


[b]Police raids[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44741273/436defd0a65f3dde6af32db12336d9955ace4010.png[/img]

Confiscation of property, fines, employee arrests -- the law can be hard on criminals, but it's even harder on those who cross the police chief. Who wants to urgently hide a sports car at the bottom of a pond, or kick all the illegals out of the studio? Better to remain a good boy and a loyal friend -- or at least find an informant at the police station. After all, the police aren't obliged to go after you specifically. There's plenty of other film studios in the neighborhood.

Or maybe it's time to put an end to this outrageous corruption once and for all, and restore order to the city?




In a forthcoming gameplay video, we'll share some of the above in greater detail, but even this is just a peek. You'll have advanced release customization options, a bag of assorted PR tricks, complicated competitors’ behavior, major historical events, detailed analytics... 

We'll make sure that the possibilities feel limitless, and the game world becomes really alive and dynamic.

Stay tuned!

notes.notes:

Your film unexpectedly became the highest-grossing picture of 1959. Where do you go from here? Of course, you capitalize on your success by cutting all possible corners and making an epically monstrous sequel! After all, that's exactly what our latest video is all about. In Hollywood Animal, you run a movie studio over the course of decades, and you're free to grow it however you please — even if it means turning it into a soulless corporate juggernaut.

[i]“There's something strangely satisfying about doing things in games that you hate seeing done in real life,"[/i] say the developers from Weappy. [i]"You might not find a single cinephile who rejoices in assembly-line filmmaking. But when you find yourself in the manager’s chair, responsible for the survival of a business, like you do in our game, all those time-tested tropes and outrageous cliches suddenly gain a new appeal."[/i]
